- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline (e.g., +10%+ then -10%+), correct by smoothing the peak and reducing overshoot by 5–15%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and model forecasts rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in downward momentum.
- Model often overestimates mean price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply downward bias of 2–5% if sentiment is ≤0.5.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to ignore it; adjust forecast to align with recent trend direction.
- When sentiment is high and price is near recent high, model often overcorrects downward; apply upward bias of 2–5% to prevent premature reversal.
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome by 3–5% over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to reflect diminishing momentum.
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model tends to overfit short-term volatility; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% in 30-day horizon.
